newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen ruling party secures election landslide.
newsitem.headline: Yemen ruling party secures election landslide.

text.p: Yemen's ruling General Peoples Congress (GPC) was assured of a sweeping victory on Friday as election results were announced for all but eight seats of the country's 301-member parliament.
A statement by Yemen's Supreme Election Committee said the GPC had won 186 seats while the Islah Party, the GPC's Islamist junior coalition partner and main rival, held 50 seats.
It said 52 seats went to independents and five seats to two opposition parties. Vote-counting continued for the remaining eight seats in the country's first parliamentary poll since a 1994 civil war.
Islah has accused the Supreme Elections Committee of bias, threatening court action.
A security official said on Friday a policeman who was among four people wounded in a shooting incident outside a vote-counting centre on Wednesday had died.
The death raised to at least 22 the number of people killed in violence linked to last Sunday's poll.

In united Yemen's first elections in 1993, the GPC won 123 seats, Islah 62 and the Yemen Socialist Party 56. Independents won 47 seats while the rest went to Baathist and Nasserite parties. The country was formed in 1990 by a merger of conservative North Yemen and Marxist South Yemen.
